title: Vector decoding after encoding
statement: Suppose a reader and writer for values in a type $A$ satisfy the following property: reading the encoding of any value followed by any suffix returns that value and suffix. Then, for every natural number $n$, every vector $f$ of $n$ values in $A$, and every bit string $x$, reading the concatenated encodings of $f(0),\ldots,f(n-1)$ followed by $x$ succeeds and returns $f$ and $x$.
hypotheses_covered: Reading any encoded value followed by any suffix returns that value and suffix
replaced:
Let a field reader and a field writer for values in a type $A$ be given such
that reading from any written value followed by any suffix returns exactly that
value and suffix.  Then for every $n$, every vector $f$ indexed by
$\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, and every bit string $x$, the length-$n$ vector reader
applied to the concatenation of the written entries $f(0), \dots, f(n-1)$ in
order, followed by $x$, succeeds and returns $(f, x)$.
